nonBlockingFindings: F11 LOW pipeline.ts:270-276 + upstream/classify.ts:89-95,111-118: the visitor-claim refund also covers reason "malformed" and 200+error body. Unlike 5xx/429/402, these outcomes are attacker-influenceable: the candidate text is attacker-controlled, so a prompt-injection or odd input that makes the free model return non-JSON or schema-invalid output gets the per-visitor req/doc quota refunded while one provider call and one global unit are consumed. Effect: one cookie can drain the global cap (35/day) alone instead of being stopped at 8 requests/24 per IP; bounded by the global cap, the 6/min in-isolate pre-limit and free-only (zero spend). Not a new class beyond what two IPs can already do, so LOW. Fix before PAID_FALLBACK_ENABLED or Phase 10: refund visitor claims only for 5xx/429/402/timeout/network, keep them on malformed and 200+error (or keep the seen marker), and add a test.

F12 LOW pipeline.ts:254-255 + limits/policy.ts:121-156: visitorMark = claims.mark() - 1 is correct today (claimAi pushes reqV, seen, docV, docIp, then global; claimOcr pushes ocrV, ocrIp, then global; the spend token is taken later, after the mark) but the invariant is implicit. Reordering or adding a claim after global in claimAi/claimOcr silently refunds the global counter or keeps a visitor claim. Add a guard comment at both call sites in policy.ts ("global MUST be the last token pushed; pipeline.refundBefore(mark - 1) depends on it") and a test for the invariant (last token of a successful claimAi and claimOcr is the global key) plus an OCR provider-failure test (visitor ocr pages refunded, global pages kept). Better: tag tokens by scope in Claims and add refundVisitorScoped() so no index arithmetic is needed. Current tests cover the AI path only.

F14 LOW pipeline.ts:284-288: a BreakerPort.trip() write failure is logged and swallowed, so with a persisted 04b breaker a failed write leaves the breaker open (read fails closed, write fails open) and the next request can reach a paid model again. 04b contract: on trip() failure also set the in-isolate memory trip, or make the default composition memory + persistent.

dvJudgements.DV1: ACCEPT with follow-up. Residual: one IP can sustain at most 3 cookies x 8 requests = 24 requests/day (each cookie needs its own Turnstile solve), vs 35/day global cap; two IPs exhaust the cap. A per-IP request counter would only raise the attacker count from about 2 to about 5 IPs, so it is not a material control and there is zero spend exposure on free-only. The 12-call budget is plan-imposed, not a platform limit; revisit in 04b (D1 batch or budget 14).

findingStatus.F1: RESOLVED. After dispatch a client abort keeps ALL claims (test: stream-holdopen abort AFTER dispatch asserts zero refunds, unchanged counters, global=1). Provider failures refund visitor-scoped claims only and keep global + spend; pre-dispatch abort and 400/401/403/413/415/422 refund everything. The repeat dispatch+disconnect abuse path is closed: each disconnect now burns the caller own req/doc quota and the global counter. See F11 for the one residual refund loop.
